sources.note: Builds prefix trees of semantically equivalent reasoning statements and measures how RLVR changes a model's preference between branches, finding the entropy collapse is not stylistic — the collapse is stronger for semantically distinct continuations than for syntactic variants of the same statement.
sources.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

sources.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
sources.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

sources.note: Shows that GRPO's per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure — a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass proportional to how often it is sampled — and rebalances it by a rarity exponent over a partition built from deterministic cue signatures rather than a judge model.
sources.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

sources.note: Explores in weight space rather than token space during RLVR by sampling policies from a variational posterior at rollout time, and introduces a training-time exploration metric -- how often a method produces a correct rollout on a prompt where GRPO produced none -- because entropy and pass@k cannot tell exploration from degeneration.
sources.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

sources.note: Shows that selecting the most confident rollout can be worse than picking at random, because uniformly high confidence signals a failure to explore rather than a well-supported answer, and replaces maximisation with a temporal criterion that penalises early certainty while requiring late certainty.
sources.title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling

sources.note: Finds that a fact successfully unlearned from a multimodal model's final answer can still be reproduced in its reasoning trace, far more in natively RL-trained models than in their base versions, and uses the token-level entropy signature RL leaves behind as a training-free control signal for redirecting the trace at decoding time.
sources.title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection

sources.note: Switches to soft-embedding latent reasoning only at low-confidence steps, keeping discrete decoding elsewhere, and pushes the soft embeddings away from the top token to stop them collapsing.
sources.title: SeLaR: Selective Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

sources.note: Tests the claim that continuous chain-of-thought lets a model hold several candidate solutions at once, and finds it holds only for models trained from scratch: off-the-shelf models collapse a superposed input to a single token within a few layers, and fine-tuned latent reasoners solve the task in one forward pass and copy the answer through the latent slots.
sources.title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models

sources.note: Argues that Shannon entropy is the wrong criterion for picking which tokens to train on in RLVR, and selects tokens instead by the Jensen-Shannon divergence of their logit distribution from the group average, updating only the top 10% of these 'unique' tokens.
sources.title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
sources.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

sources.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
sources.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

sources.note: Recasts entropy collapse as an imbalance of 'entropy flow' — tokens whose update lowers entropy persistently outweigh those that raise it — and rebalances the two sets with a closed-form coefficient computed from each batch, without reference policies or entropy bonuses.
sources.title: Understanding and Preventing Entropy Collapse in RLVR with On-Policy Entropy Flow Optimization

sources.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
sources.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

sources.note: A systematic empirical study of entropy in RLVR that finds entropy correlates with response diversity but only weakly and inconsistently with accuracy, identifies clipping thresholds, off-policy updates and data diversity as its drivers, and argues positive-advantage tokens are what collapses it.
sources.title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Introduces EDIS, a trajectory-level score that measures how unstably token entropy evolves during generation, and uses it to select better reasoning rollouts at inference and to curate training samples in RL.
sources.title: EDIS: Diagnosing LLM Reasoning via Entropy Dynamics

sources.note: Proves that an entropy bonus permanently moves the stationary point of RL training while covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once its coefficient is annealed, and that the bonus shrinks the stability margin where the targeted methods leave it intact.
sources.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

result.definition: The fall of policy entropy to near zero within a few hundred steps of reinforcement learning on reasoning tasks, and across 16 sources one of the archive's best-quantified training phenomena. It is front-loaded: across 11 runs of 2,400 gradient steps, 73 percent of entropy consumption and 76 percent of performance gain occur in the first 200 steps and the first 800 account for over 93 percent of gain with 94 percent of entropy loss, so more than two-thirds of training yields marginal returns. It coincides with the highest training reward, which several sources read as premature exploitation of a narrow set of high-reward patterns. The interpretive question the corpus takes seriously is what collapsed. A measured fall is compatible with the policy having calcified merely stylistic choices or with its having pruned genuinely distinct inferential pathways, and the source that separates them finds the collapse significantly stronger in a semantic contrast than a syntactic one -- so it is inferences rather than phrasing. That same source shows the compensating gain and the cost in one measurement: the trained policy's entropy collapses correctly where only one continuation is legal, and with illegal continuations masked away the flatter distilled policy outperforms it by about 60 percent. Many mitigations exist -- clipping variants, covariance-based penalties, entropy regularisation, strict on-policy updating, and restricting updates to high-entropy tokens -- and the corpus's caution about them is that one paper's largest reported share of the gain came from switching to strict on-policy training rather than from the entropy mechanism it credits, and that one theoretical account depends on the advantage of tokens never sampled, which most algorithms cannot estimate.
